title: Compiler Construction
description: Translators and the structure of a compiler, grammars and the Chomsky hierarchy, regular expressions and finite automata, lexical, syntax and semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimization, code generation and error handling. Built from the Ibadan Distance Learning course material for CSC 431 and past papers from 2016/17 to 2018/19.

topics.title: Translators and the Compiler Overview
topics.summary: Translators convert high-level or assembly programs into machine code; compilers translate the whole program at once, interpreters one statement at a time, and assemblers translate assembly language. A compiler has an analysis front end (scanner, syntax and semantic analysers) and a synthesis back end (preparation for code generation, code generation), all using tables of information such as the symbol table.
subtopics: High-level, assembly and machine languages
Compilers, interpreters and assemblers: similarities and differences
Linkers and loaders
Analysis and synthesis phases; the symbol table
Phases and passes; single-pass and multi-pass compilers
Compiler-compilers, cross compilers, source-to-source compilers; qualities of a good compiler

topics.title: Linguistic Analysis and Grammars
topics.summary: A language is a set of sentences over an alphabet, described by a grammar G = (VN, VT, P, S) of non-terminals, terminals, productions and a start symbol. Chomsky's hierarchy runs from Type 0 (unrestricted) through Type 1 (context sensitive) and Type 2 (context free) to Type 3 (regular), and some context-free grammars are ambiguous.
subtopics: Alphabet, string, sentence, V* and V+
The four tuples of a grammar G = (VN, VT, P, S)
Sentences and sentential forms; derivation
Chomsky Types 0, 1, 2 and 3
Ambiguous context-free grammars
Precedence, operator and operator precedence grammars

topics.title: Regular Expressions and Finite Automata
topics.summary: Regular expressions specify the patterns of tokens using union, concatenation and Kleene closure, with * binding tightest and | loosest. Finite automata recognise those patterns, and the scanner uses the longest match rule to choose between possible tokens.
subtopics: Regular languages and regular grammars
Union, concatenation and Kleene closure
Precedence and associativity of operators
x*, x+, x? and character classes
Tokens as regular expressions: identifiers, decimals
Finite automata (Q, Σ, q0, qf, δ) and the longest match rule

topics.title: Programming Language Structure and Lexical Analysis
topics.summary: Before building a compiler, its designer studies the language's syntax and semantics, tokens, data elements, binding, operators, coercion, storage management and parameter passing. The scanner then breaks the source program into tokens, builds their tables and passes an internal form to the parser.
subtopics: Syntax and semantics; the character set
Tokens and BNF notation
Data elements, identifiers and binding
Operators and coercion of data types
Storage management and parameter passing
The scanner's tasks and routines (Get_Next_Char, Mark)

topics.title: Syntax Analysis (Parsing)
topics.summary: The parser checks the token sequence against a context-free grammar and builds a parse tree, using leftmost or rightmost derivations. Grammars are prepared by removing left recursion and left factoring and computing FIRST and FOLLOW sets, and parsing is top-down (predictive, recursive descent) or bottom-up (shift-reduce, LR, operator precedence).
subtopics: Tasks of the parser
Leftmost and rightmost derivation; parse trees
Associativity and precedence
Left recursion and left factoring
FIRST and FOLLOW sets
Top-down and bottom-up parsing; the operator precedence algorithm

topics.title: Semantic Analysis and Intermediate Code
topics.summary: Semantic analysis checks meaning that parsing cannot, such as declarations, types and scope, using attribute grammars with synthesized and inherited attributes. It rewrites accepted code in an intermediate language: Polish (postfix) notation, quadruples or triples, using routines such as LOOK_UP, INSERT, ENTER and CHECK_TYPE.
subtopics: Functions of semantic analysis and semantic errors
Static and dynamic semantic analysis
Attribute grammars: synthesized and inherited attributes
Polish (postfix) notation and stack evaluation
Quadruples, triples and indirect triples
Semantic routines: LOOK_UP, INSERT, ENTER, CHECK_TYPE

topics.title: Code Optimization, Code Generation and Error Handling
topics.summary: Optimization improves code without changing its meaning, at the source, intermediate and machine level, for example by removing redundant instructions and unreachable code and optimizing loops. The code generator maps intermediate code to target instructions using register and address descriptors, and the error handler detects, reports and recovers from lexical, syntactic, semantic and logical errors.
subtopics: Rules of optimization; machine-independent and machine-dependent
Peephole optimizations and strength reduction
Loop optimization
Code generation: instruction selection, register allocation, descriptors
Four alternatives for generating object code; bootstrapping
Error classes and recovery: panic mode, statement mode, error productions, global correction
